# Results index

*Generated by `backend/eval/build_results_readme.py` — do not edit by hand.*
Every figure below is read out of the JSON in this directory. Re-run the
generator after a new result lands.

## Which directory is authoritative

The two directories hold near-identical filenames and that has confused
readers, so it is stated plainly:

| directory | what ran there | use it for |
|---|---|---|
| `results/` | laptop + free hosted tier, 4 GB VRAM | the scale runs and the shipped-rule replay |
| `results/dgx_fullscale/` | campus **NVIDIA GB10 (DGX Spark)**, 119 GB unified | the paired controlled experiments that need a big model resident |

They are deliberately **not merged**. They are different platforms and their
verdicts disagree — §4.10 measures that disagreement as a result in its own
right, so blending them would destroy the very effect being reported.

## 1. The verdict rule — the single largest effect we control

`weighted_aggregation.json` · 10 random dev/test splits, n=233 rows

| rule | false-alarm rate | precision | recall | F1 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| OR-gate (any specialist flags) | **64.8% ± 5.4** | 0.563 ± 0.021 | 0.938 ± 0.020 | 0.703 ± 0.017 |
| Pooled noisy-OR threshold (**shipped**) | **27.4% ± 7.8** | 0.733 ± 0.043 | 0.824 ± 0.101 | 0.770 ± 0.033 |

Held-out test split, so the threshold was not fitted on it:

| rule | tp | fp | tn | fn | FPR | F1 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| OR-gate | 51 | 43 | 19 | 4 | 69.4% | 0.685 |
| noisy-OR threshold | 48 | 19 | 43 | 7 | 30.6% | 0.787 |

The weighted rule wins **9 of 10** splits. Per-class weighting beats a flat threshold on only 3 of them, so the reported gain is attributed to **thresholding**, not to the weights: `threshold_only` reaches F1 0.790 against the weighted rule's 0.770.

## 3. False alarms by provenance of the "safe" label

**The lead result.** Same tool, same seed, same machine, same contracts —
the only thing that changes between rows is *how the safe label was
obtained*.

| safe tier | n | fp (shipped) | **false-alarm rate, shipped rule** | (OR-gate, for reference) |
|---|--:|--:|---|---|
| Audited libraries (OZ/Solady) | 172 | 27 | **15.7% [11.0, 21.9]** | 49.4% [42.0, 56.8] |
| Audit-reviewed, clean | 240 | 90 | **37.5% [31.6, 43.8]** | 66.2% [60.1, 71.9] |
| Real-world, no bug reported | 191 | 63 | **33.0% [26.7, 39.9]** | 58.6% [51.6, 65.4] |

Audited libraries separate cleanly from both weaker tiers. The two
weaker tiers have overlapping intervals and are **not** distinguishable
from each other — the effect is two-level, not a monotonic gradient,
and an earlier version of this work overstated it as three steps.

| vulnerable tier | n | tp (OR-gate) | detection rate (95% Wilson) |
|---|--:|--:|---|
| Curated vulnerable (SmartBugs-style) | 214 | 185 | 86.4% [81.2, 90.4] |
| Injected vulnerability | 170 | 152 | 89.4% [83.9, 93.2] |
| Real audit-report findings | 167 | 118 | 70.7% [63.4, 77.0] |

## 4. Head-to-head vs Slither, identical contracts

`slither_bench.json` · rule: `NO-GO iff >=1 High/Medium impact detector`

| | Slither | ThirdEye |
|---|--:|--:|
| contracts presented | 150 | 150 |
| answered | **46** | **150** |
| abstained (could not compile) | 104 | 0 |
| precision, where it answers | **0.941** | 0.712 |
| recall, where it answers | 0.889 | 0.808 |
| tp / fp / tn / fn | 32 / 2 / 8 / 4 | — |

**Read this honestly.** Where Slither answers it is *more precise than
we are* — 34 flagged, 2 wrong, a 5.9% false-discovery rate that
corroborates the 10.9% its own paper reports (Feist et al., WETSEB'19).
Our advantage is coverage, not accuracy: it answered 46 of 150 contracts.
All 104 abstentions were diagnosed with `solc` directly
(`slither_failure_audit.json`); exactly **one** was attributable to our
toolchain. Durieux et al. (ICSE'20) independently measure Slither at
20/115 (17%) across categories, which is the same coverage story on a
different corpus.

## 5. Head-to-head vs GPTScan (ICSE'24)

`dgx_fullscale/web3bugs_gptscan.json` · contest-level, any-slice-positive

| | value |
|---|--:|
| contests scored | 63 |
| contests detected | 62 |
| contest-level recall | 98.4% [91.5, 99.7] |
| median latency | 226.9 s |

On the **34 gradable projects both tools were asked about**, ThirdEye
detects 33 and GPTScan 31, and the intervals **overlap** — no detection
difference is demonstrated, and it is reported that way rather than as a
win. Precision is not computable on this bucket: every project in it is
positive, so there is no negative class. It stays on the balanced tiers
in table 3.

## 6. Paired controlled experiments

Each varies exactly **one** thing; arms share contract ids, seed, model
digests and machine. Significance by McNemar on the paired table.

| experiment | variable | paired n | result | p |
|---|---|--:|---|--:|
| Context window | `num_ctx` 4,096 -> 16,384 | 20 scored of 36 | 12 verdicts corrected vs 2 broken | **0.016** |
| Model capacity | 3B -> `llama3.1:8b` on 3 semantic roles | 232 | accuracy 0.651 vs 0.625 (laptop) | see paper |
| Batch parallelism | `num_parallel=1` control | 227 | cross-machine agreement 0.727 | 0.75 (n.s.) |

The context result is the headline: raising `num_ctx` corrected **12**
verdicts and broke **2**, p = 0.016. Ollama truncates silently, and
abstentions are excluded from scoring — so the misconfiguration
*removed rows* rather than lowering any score. It is measured on the
vulnerable class; the safe-class arm is still running and may move
the 29.9% figure, which is stated as an open risk rather than hidden.

## 7. Seed variance

| seed | n | scored | precision | recall | F1 | FPR |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 | 90 | 74 | 0.653 | 0.800 | 0.719 | 37.8% |
| 2 | 90 | 81 | 0.711 | 0.762 | 0.736 | 28.9% |

**No mean ± std is reported across all three seeds, deliberately.**
Seeds 1 and 2 are 90-contract stratified samples (15 per tier); seed 0 is
the full 1154-contract run. Averaging figures computed on different
populations would blend two samples into one number, which is defect #6
in the paper's silent-failure list. The two comparable seeds are shown
side by side and the spread is left visible.

## Reproducing any of this

Every run is checkpointed per contract, so each table can be re-scored
without re-running inference:

```bash
python -m eval.run_benchmark --report-only     # tables 2 and 3
python -m eval.run_slither_bench --report-only # table 4
python -m eval.run_web3bugs --report-only --gptscan-set  # table 5
python backend/eval/build_results_readme.py    # regenerate this file
```

Confidence intervals are **Wilson**, never Wald: several of these rates sit
at or near 0 or 1, where the Wald interval collapses to zero width.
